I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is still the most practical way for me to make the year work. I already have winter wheat in the field at the start of the season, so I will push that crop through spring with steady fertilizer, two irrigations if water allows, and tight weed and disease control. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize on the same land because the season is short and I do not want to lose soil moisture or planting time. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I care more about stable yield and stress tolerance than saving a little seed cost. I will not spread myself across too many crops. At my age and with my conditions, I would rather run one familiar rotation well than manage several smaller crops poorly. I will keep tillage simple, use fertilizer at moderate rates, irrigate only when the crop response is clear, and spray based on the common local pest and disease pressure.
